@geoffkizer Closing as duplicate of #24693. Please let's know if you think otherwise.
I'm reopening this because I want to get the API reviewed, and this seems like the best issue to do it with (as opposed to editing the issue it's marked as a dupe of).
@stephentoub I marked this as api-ready-for-review. If you don't agree please let me know and remove the label.
@geoffkizer do you see this is different than #24693? I am not opposing the proposal here. Just checking if we should close one of them if both same issue.
It's the same issue.
Added an overload of Register with `bool useSynchronizationContext` to match existing API.
ok, I closed the other one and keeping this active.
@stephentoub is it a reasonable proposal to proceed with?

Yes.

We might consider swapping the order of the arguments to the delegate, so that in all delegates the object state is first.

I'd also be happy with us not proactively adding:
```C#
public CancellationTokenRegistration Register(Action<CancellationToken, object> callback, object state, bool useSynchronizationContext);
```
and only adding it if someone actually comes forth with a good use case of it.  Passing true for useSynchronizationContext is very rare; I think I can count the number of times I've seen it on one hand.

Otherwise, it should be fine, and while there'll be a tad more overhead added due to needing to now check what kind of delegate is being used, it's unlikely to be measurable.
@tarekgh, I've edited your post above to also factor in nullable reference types.
LGTM

> Why is the method signature forcing object? type for the state? Wouldn't be better to have something like this instead?

It would make the implementation much more expensive (e.g. right now the CancellationTokenSource can cache the objects used to store the registration, but that caching becomes a lot more challenging when it needs to differentiate by T), there's slightly more cost at runtime due to generic dictionaries when the state is a reference type, the vast, vast majority of usage has a reference type state such that the T saves very little in usability (just a cast) and nothing measurable in perf, ...

Yes, I'm concern about usability for seasonal developers. The implementation would stay the same but instead of asking every user of this API to do an odd explicit cast with bang we could cast inside the API.

> How would the delegate be invoked?

Good point.
